brief.subject: Midterms reset the tax agenda; IRS tweaks QOZ reporting rules
brief.headline: New Congress Reshapes Tax Outlook as IRS Adjusts Opportunity Zone Reporting Rules
brief.dek: Midterm results shift Congress and the tax agenda, the IRS corrects proposed opportunity zone reporting rules, and a scholarship credit hearing goes phone-only.
brief.lede: The 2026 midterms flipped control of Congress, making a sweeping tax bill less likely and narrow bipartisan fixes more plausible.

sections.heading: Midterms Redraw the Tax Map
bullets: Congressional control changed hands in the 2026 midterms, resetting the federal tax policy agenda.
Large, sweeping tax packages now face longer odds, so avoid building plans around major overhauls.
Targeted bipartisan measures may gain room, which could still bring narrower changes affecting small firms.

sections.heading: IRS Fixes Opportunity Zone Reporting Draft
bullets: The IRS issued corrections to proposed rules REG-116506-25, first published September 11, 2026.
The rules would require qualified opportunity funds to file information returns and send statements to investors who dispose of interests.
Qualified opportunity zone businesses would also owe statements to funds holding their interests, adding new reporting work for affected owners.

sections.heading: Scholarship Credit Hearing Goes Phone-Only
bullets: The December 15, 2026, 10 a.m. ET hearing on REG-117199-25 will now be held by telephone only.
The proposal covers a non-refundable federal credit for contributions to scholarship granting organizations funding K-12 education.
Clients weighing these donations should watch for final guidance before counting on the credit.

sections.heading: IRS Seeks Input on Withholding Paperwork
bullets: The IRS is taking public comments on the burden of its QI, WP and WT application and account system.
The request falls under the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995 and mainly concerns foreign intermediaries handling withholding.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Information Reporting Regarding Qualified Opportunity Zones and Updated Qualified Opportunity Fund Certification and Decertification Procedures; Correction
items.snippet: This document contains corrections to the proposed regulations (REG-116506-25), published in the Federal Register on September 11, 2026. These proposed regulations would implement new statutory requirements for qualified opportunity funds to file information returns with the IRS and furnish statements to investors who dispose of investments in those entities and for qualified opportunity zone businesses to furnish statements to qualified opportunity funds that hold interests in them.
